description: Replace the dashboard-like homepage with an information-first editorial portfolio anchored by a scroll-driven optimization landscape and Damon's real work, research, writing, and contact details.

userStories.title: Build the identity-first optimization landscape hero
userStories.description: As a visitor, I can immediately understand who Damon is, what he does, and where to go next while the supplied landscape guides attention without obscuring the content.
acceptanceCriteria: The first viewport clearly presents Damon Guo-Shiyu, LLM Engineer at Alibaba in Hangzhou, and his focus on agent systems, post-training, evaluation, and agentic RL using real repository information.
Visible actions link to selected work and contact; no terminal, live clock, fake runtime state, synthetic metrics, or dashboard copy remains in the hero.
At 1440x1000, identity, current role, focus, and both primary actions are visible above the fold and the supplied optimization landscape reads as a layered 2.5D scene.
At 390x844, primary text is unclipped, the landscape does not cover content or block touch scrolling, and document.scrollWidth is no greater than document.clientWidth.
With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the same information and actions remain visible, the landscape is composed as a static image, and continuous GSAP/p5 motion is skipped.
The responsive landscape base image remains visible if p5 fails, dynamically loads p5 when motion is allowed, and cleans up p5, GSAP contexts, listeners, and ScrollTriggers on unmount.

The original 2944x1648 PNG remains unchanged as provenance with SHA-256 fe8f717fa83332050cdbb98d123caf087ecb7857b86e301f041d4aa37abbe711; production markup uses optimization-landscape-2200.webp for desktop and optimization-landscape-1100.webp for mobile rather than downloading the 5.4 MB PNG by default.

The 2200px desktop WebP is no larger than 128000 bytes and the 1100px mobile WebP is no larger than 48000 bytes, and both preserve the source's black negative space, copper ridge, light path, and terrain silhouette in visual review.

Task 1 foundation verification proves npm run build and npm run lint pass after dependency installation and verifies source and derivative identity, dimensions, and byte budgets; Vite asset emission is deferred until this story imports the responsive derivatives, after which the production build must emit the referenced image assets.

Desktop, mobile, and reduced-motion screenshots are reviewed by Codex; the review first literally describes what is visible, then judges information clarity, visual harmony, and whether the light/3D effect guides rather than distracts, and records PASS.
npm run build and npm run lint exit successfully with no new errors.

userStories.title: Present selected work as editorial case studies
userStories.description: As a visitor, I can scan three representative projects and understand their context, Damon's contribution, and the outcome without operating a carousel or dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: The homepage shows exactly three representative entries sourced from src/data/projects.js, each with its real title, truthful context or problem, contribution, outcome, and category.
All project information is readable without interaction, a clear link reaches /projects, keyboard focus is visible, and no horizontal carousel is required.
At 1440x1000, the selected-work hierarchy and at least the active project outcome are legible while the restrained light marker supports the reading order.
At 390x844, entries follow DOM order in one readable column and document.scrollWidth is no greater than document.clientWidth.
With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, all project content remains visible and the section light marker does not use continuous or scroll-scrubbed motion.

Desktop, mobile, and reduced-motion screenshots are reviewed by Codex; the review first literally describes the visible project titles and outcomes, then judges clarity, hierarchy, and whether the light effect supports or obscures them, and records PASS.
npm run build and npm run lint exit successfully with no new errors.

userStories.title: Tell the research and experience story
userStories.description: As a visitor, I can understand Damon's career and research trajectory as a chronological editorial narrative grounded in the existing profile data.
acceptanceCriteria: The section uses timelineData and aboutProfile from src/data/about.js and visibly includes Alibaba, MSRA, NUS, UNSW, and the real research or publication count.
Chronology is understandable without opening cards: the current role is emphasized, earlier entries are progressively quieter, and education and research remain factually clear.
At 1440x1000, the current role and relationship between research and experience are visually legible without simulated control-surface UI.
At 390x844, reading order matches chronology, institution names and dates are unclipped, and document.scrollWidth is no greater than document.clientWidth.
With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the entire career path remains visible and any entrance stagger resolves immediately without scroll-scrubbed motion.

Desktop, mobile, and reduced-motion screenshots are reviewed by Codex; the review first literally describes the institutions, dates, and emphasis visible, then states Damon's inferred career path and judges clarity and visual harmony, and records PASS.
npm run build and npm run lint exit successfully with no new errors.
userStories.notes: Uses existing about data without inventing claims.

userStories.title: Unify writing, contact, navigation, and footer
userStories.description: As a visitor, I can discover Damon's latest writing and reach him through a coherent editorial conclusion and accessible navigation.
acceptanceCriteria: The writing section uses real entries from src/data/posts.js and visibly preserves each shown title, date, excerpt, reading time, and a working link to /blog.

The contact conclusion shows the existing email address plus only personal social URLs verified as belonging to Damon through an authoritative source or Damon's direct confirmation; a reachable URL alone is not identity verification.
Every displayed personal social URL has recorded identity-verification evidence; any unverified channel is removed or omitted rather than preserved, and no replacement identity or URL is invented.
The currently configured LinkedIn slug shengyue-guan-1a7b3226b is treated as suspicious and must not be accepted as Damon's or displayed unless independent identity verification is obtained.

Navigation preserves the skip link, theme toggle, active-route indication, mobile menu, Escape-to-close behavior, and visible keyboard focus while removing the live clock, online pulse, and dashboard capsule language.
At 1440x1000 section screenshots, writing and contact read as the conclusion of one personal portfolio rather than unrelated product cards.
At 390x844, post metadata and contact channels remain readable, the mobile menu is usable, and document.scrollWidth is no greater than document.clientWidth.
With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, writing, contact, navigation, and footer retain their full hierarchy without required motion or delayed content.

Desktop, mobile, and reduced-motion screenshots are reviewed by Codex; the review first literally describes visible posts, dates, contact channels, and navigation, then judges information clarity, cohesion, and visual harmony, and records PASS.
npm run build and npm run lint exit successfully with no new errors.
userStories.notes: Preserves existing routes and accessibility contracts.

userStories.title: Complete full-site regression and visual acceptance
userStories.description: As Damon, I can ship the editorial homepage knowing its real information, routes, responsiveness, accessibility, and attention-guiding motion work together without regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: The complete homepage clearly communicates identity, selected work, research and experience, writing, and contact using only real repository data and no fake dashboard state.
Existing /about, /projects, /blog, /blog/:slug, and /uses routes load and retain their expected content, links, theme behavior, and navigation contracts.
A full scroll pass at 1440x1000 covers hero, selected work, research, writing, and contact with no clipped content, console errors, broken images, or interaction regressions.
A full scroll pass at 390x844 has no blocked scrolling or clipped primary text, all touch targets remain usable, and document.scrollWidth is no greater than document.clientWidth.
With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, every section and action remains available, the landscape is static, and no continuous or scroll-scrubbed animation is required to understand the page.

Final desktop, mobile, and reduced-motion screenshot sets are reviewed by Codex; for every screenshot the review first literally describes what is visible, then judges information clarity, visual harmony, personal-portfolio cohesion, and whether light/3D guidance distracts, and records PASS.
Browser verification finds no console errors during mount, full scroll, route changes, mobile menu interaction, or unmount.
npm run build and npm run lint exit successfully, and Ralph marks all five stories passes true only after their criteria and screenshot reviews are satisfied.
